newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS confirms Canada long-term ratings at AA+.
newsitem.headline: CBRS confirms Canada long-term ratings at AA+.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Thursday it reaffirmed its ratings for the Government of Canada's long-term debt at AA+ and short-term at A-1+ with a stable rating outlook.
The Montreal-based ratings agency said it reaffirmed the ratings because the Canadian government surpassed its deficiet target for the third straight year.
It said the stable outlook was maintained because the government continued to reduce its program spending and CBRS believed the government would likely balance its budget in fiscal year 1999-00.
The Canadian government said in its fiscal 1997-98 budget that it expected to cut its deficit to C$9.0 billion or one percent of gross domestic product by fiscal 1998-99.
"Although the federal government is significantly ahead of its 1997-98 deficit target, it continues to view deficit reduction as a high priority," CBRS said.

"Consequently, no wide-ranging tax cuts were introduced in this year's budget, a positive move given the federal government's C$610 billion debt which will require balanced budgets. Also, if no significant tax cuts are introduced in the next two years, in CBRS' opinion the federal government is very likely to achieve a surplus in 1999-00."
